newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey raises withholding tax on bonds income.
newsitem.headline: Turkey raises withholding tax on bonds income.

text.p: Turkey will raise the withholding tax on bonds and treasury-bill income to 12 percent from 10 percent, and postpone a plan to introduce an income tax on interest earnings from bonds and t-bills, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Friday.

"The plan to enforce a tax declaration has been postponed by one year and the withholding tax, which was put into effect on November 1, will be raised to 12 percent from 10 percent," she told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
She did not give other details.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said before the cabinet meeting that many investors had complained about the tax declaration plan and said they would prefer to pay more withholding tax than go through the "tedious" task of filling out tax forms.
"We have complaints from our citizens that they are ready to to pay more withholding tax instead of the tedious task of filling out tax forms to declare their interest income," he said.

Turkey imposed the 10-percent withholding tax on the interest income from treasury bills and bonds to be issued from November 1 with 1997 maturity as part of the government's revenue raising packages.
An income tax exemption on government bond and treasury bill yields will expire on December 31.
